integrity: Every private leaf forces selection of itself or its support vertex, giving a lower bound of \(n\); the semipaired partition forces even cardinality. For the upper bound, a longest-path leaf-reduction proves that the square of every tree has a matching of size \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor\). Applying this to a spanning tree of the base graph pairs all original vertices when \(n\) is even and all but one when \(n\) is odd; in the odd case the unmatched support vertex is paired with its own private leaf. The standalone verifier exhaustively computes the true corona optimum for every connected labeled graph through order five and separately checks the constructive matching lemma on all Prüfer-coded trees through order seven.
scientific_limitations: The theorem treats the one-leaf corona \(G\circ K_1\) of a connected base graph and does not claim a formula for general corona products \(G\circ H\).
Disconnected base graphs are outside the claim and may require componentwise parity handling.

The 2018 introducing journal article predates the exact-day public preprints used here, but no day-resolved public preprint date for that article was verified; the first_public_date field therefore uses the earliest exact public posting actually verified, 2019-04-01.
Finite exhaustive verification covers connected labeled base graphs through order five and is corroborative rather than the arbitrary-order proof.
A differently phrased or non-indexed treatment of the same corona family may exist.
title: Semipaired domination of leaf coronas
